paper_title: Towards Predicting Any Human Trajectory In Context
caption: Performance of random example selection and the proposed STES at varying numbers of in-context examples with a larger number of examples

model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates the performance of two methods—ST-ES (proposed method) and Random example selection—measured by the metric minFDE₂₀ (lower is better) as the number of in-context examples increases from 0 to 15. The x-axis, labeled “Number of Examples,” uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 15 with integer tick marks spaced at intervals of 5. The y-axis, labeled “minFDE₂₀ (←)”, also uses a linear scale, ranging from 0.85 to 1.05, with major tick marks at intervals of 0.05. The ST-ES method is represented by a blue line with circular markers; it starts at a minFDE₂₀ value of approximately 1.05 when the number of examples is 0, drops sharply to about 0.86 at 1 example, then stabilizes between 0.82 and 0.84 for 2 to 12 examples, and slightly increases to around 0.83 at 15 examples. The Random method is represented by an orange line with circular markers; it begins at approximately 1.03 at 0 examples, decreases gradually to about 0.97 at 5 examples, and then remains relatively stable between 0.96 and 0.98 up to 15 examples. The plot demonstrates that ST-ES consistently achieves lower minFDE₂₀ values than Random across all numbers of examples, indicating superior performance.
model_annotations.German: The plot illustrates the performance of two methods—ST-ES (blue line with circular markers) and Random (orange line with circular markers)—in terms of minFDE₂₀ (a metric with no units, as indicated by “(–)”) as the number of in-context examples varies from 0 to 15. The x-axis is labeled “Number of Examples” and uses a linear scale ranging from 0 to 15, with tick marks at integer intervals. The y-axis is labeled “minFDE₂₀ (–)” and also uses a linear scale, ranging from 0.85 to 1.05, with tick marks at 0.05 intervals. The ST-ES method starts at a minFDE₂₀ of approximately 1.05 when the number of examples is 0, then drops sharply to about 0.85 at 2 examples, and remains relatively stable between 0.83 and 0.85 for the rest of the range, with a slight increase to approximately 0.84 at 15 examples. In contrast, the Random method begins at a minFDE₂₀ of about 1.03 at 0 examples, decreases gradually to around 0.97 at 5 examples, and then fluctuates slightly between 0.96 and 0.98 for the remaining examples, ending at approximately 0.97 at 15 examples. The plot includes a legend in the upper right corner identifying the two methods by color and line style.
